2d_in_3d_randomness_vis.description: An infoboard displaying 2D randomness algorithms rendered in 3D space, bridging flat visualizations with spatial understanding.
2d_in_3d_randomness_vis.name: 2D in 3D Randomness Visualization
2d_in_3d_randomness_vis.qfep_connection: The flat diagrams of chance — scatter plots, walks, histograms — stood upright in the room. The board bridges the textbook and the terrarium: what the page could only plot, the space around you performs.

GaussianBlurCircle.description: Demonstrates Gaussian blur applied to a circular region, showing how the bell curve kernel creates smooth, natural edge falloff.
GaussianBlurCircle.name: Gaussian Blur Circle
GaussianBlurCircle.qfep_connection: The bell curve applied to sight: a circle dissolving under gaussian blur, each pixel averaged with its neighbors under the curve. The same mathematics that files the draws also softens the world — distribution as a way of seeing.

GaussianBlurShader.description: GPU-accelerated Gaussian blur using a fragment shader. Real-time demonstration of the convolution kernel derived from the normal distribution.
GaussianBlurShader.name: Gaussian Blur Shader

GaussianPaintSplatter.description: Generates paint splatter patterns using Gaussian distribution, creating natural clustering around a center point with density falling off like a bell curve.
GaussianPaintSplatter.name: Gaussian Paint Splatter

MeltingBerniniScene.description: Noise-based vertex displacement applied to classical column geometry. Bernini's baroque forms dissolve under procedural noise fields.
MeltingBerniniScene.name: Melting Bernini Columns
MeltingBerniniScene.qfep_connection: Bernini's columns dissolving under noise-driven vertex displacement: the baroque — history's most deliberate style — surrendered to structured chance. The primitive of the chapter played as elegy: noise does not destroy the form, it *remembers* it while letting it go, coherence draining out neighbor by neighbor.

NoiseColors3D.description: Compares different noise 'colors' (white, pink, brown, blue) in 3D space, visualizing their distinct frequency distributions and correlation properties.
NoiseColors3D.name: Noise Colors 3D
NoiseColors3D.qfep_connection: Noise has colors: white forgets everything, pink remembers a little, brown wanders like a drunk with a heading, blue avoids itself. The gallery of temperaments — proof that 'random' is not one substance but a spectrum of relationships between a sample and its past.

RandomGaussianTexture.description: Generates textures with pixel values sampled from a Gaussian distribution, creating soft, natural-looking noise patterns.
RandomGaussianTexture.name: Random Gaussian Texture
RandomGaussianTexture.qfep_connection: The mean is hard-coded to the middle of the screen; only deviation is delegated to chance, on a leash of sixty pixels of standard deviation. What the accumulating smudge demonstrates is not randomness but its licensing — wander permitted against a promised return.

Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ.description: Applies random rotation on all three axes (X, Y, Z), creating fully randomized orientations for chaotic arrangements.
Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ.name: Random Rotate XYZ
Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ.qfep_connection: The room's namesake engine: grid cubes spun by three independent draws, one per axis. Orientation surrendered to chance while position holds — the grid keeping order in one register and losing it in another, which is the whole trick of controlled entropy.

RotateGridCubes.description: Gradient slope test with animated rotation for walkability check.
RotateGridCubes.name: Slope Gradient Cubes

VoxelNoiseROIs.description: Voxel noise with regions of interest (ROIs) — isolated volumes where different noise parameters or thresholds apply, useful for terrain biomes.
VoxelNoiseROIs.name: Voxel Noise ROIs

WhiteNoiseGallery.description: A gallery showcasing pure white noise — uniform random values with no correlation between samples. The baseline for understanding structured noise types.
WhiteNoiseGallery.name: White Noise Gallery
WhiteNoiseGallery.qfep_connection: The baseline: pure white noise, every sample a stranger to its neighbors. This is randomness before it learns to remember — the hiss the whole chapter is a departure from. Hang it first so every other room can be measured as distance from amnesia.

bell_alley.description: Constructs a corridor of cubes along Z that widens according to a Gaussian bell curve, creating a passage that narrows at the center and expands at the edges.
bell_alley.name: Bell Curve Alley

blue_noise.description: Interactive blue noise generation for high-quality random sampling and distribution
blue_noise.name: Blue Noise

dna.was: twenty-eight exported knobs and not one of them a claim: spawn_area_size, four min/max bounds, max_bubble_count, spawn_rate, three lifetime and fade durations, six light numbers, four dish dimensions, eight sound numbers. Every one is a magnitude, a rate or a colour. apply_grid_config existed and its entire body was `pass`, so every key a map could send was silently discarded, and the runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS - which was a fact about the KIND of knob, not their number.
dna.note: assay is the softbody bench family's word and its five values character for character - seventeen artifacts already ask what apparatus a specimen is surrounded by, and petri_dish_worms, the corpus's other petri dish, joined the same word on 2026-08-05. The dish is the constraint that lets the dispersion be read' - is that question stated from the inside, so a private synonym would have split one question across two vocabularies for no gain. `control` is the rung that argues hardest and argues harder here than for the worms: an empty second dish is the only thing that can turn a cloud of luck from a thing you are watching into an experiment you could disagree with. Every apparatus dimension is petri_dish_worms' absolute number divided by its AS_DISH_R of 0.16 and multiplied by this dish's own radius, so the two dishes carry the same apparatus at their own sizes instead of one carrying a scale model of the other - which is what `the siblings measure alike' has to mean when the objects are 22x apart. The one place the rungs diverge is the chart's plotted line: the sibling draws a logistic because a worm population grows, and a bubble dish has no growth curve, so this plate carries a flat-topped histogram between a marked floor and a marked ceiling - the artifact's own thesis as a picture. Fixed, never sampled: a rung that rolled dice would make every capture a different frame.
dna.fixture_note: bubble_seed is a fixture and NOT an axis. This dish costs TEN unseeded draws per bubble (three position, one size, one rise speed, two wobble, two horizontal drift, one light ballot) plus one more consumed by the dead sound gate, and it spawns ten bubbles a second, so at the 1.1 s settle five sweep frames would be five different clouds and the critic would read that noise as a confident BITE on whatever axis happened to be varying. The two drift draws used to be made inside Bubble._init, which an inner class cannot route through the outer node's generator; they moved out to spawn_bubble at exactly the point in the sequence they were made from before - after wobble_speed, before the light ballot - so the -1 stream is unchanged.

Adopting the list would mean either calling that shipped behaviour `none', which is not what the word means where it already lives, or forking the list with a sixth value - the folding_past fault, taking a word without its answers. coin_toss.name: Coin Toss

dice_throw.name: Dice Throw

env_one.name: Environment One
env_one.qfep_connection: A whole environment kitbashed by draw: parts picked, placed, and joined by chance. The room-scale claim of the chapter — not an object randomized, but a *place* that entropy furnished.

evolutionary_algorithms.description: Particle system demonstrating selection, mutation, and crossover. Populations evolve toward fitness goals through randomized genetic operations.
evolutionary_algorithms.name: Evolutionary Algorithms

dna.default: selection=culled - _winner_count() returns int(n * ELITE_FRACTION) with ELITE_FRACTION = 0.1, which is the shipped `int(particles.size() * 0.1)` unchanged, and the single-optimum path calls _evolve_toward(particles, target, delta) on the SAME array the old code sorted in place. Inside that loop nothing moved: the same beeline at 2.0 with the same +/-0.5 jitter, the same gold Color(1,0.8,0.2) at radius 0.08, the same 0.9 damping plus 0.5 follow plus 0.3 mutation, the same rank_ratio colour ramp and the same 0.05 - 0.02*rank radius, in the same order, so the random stream is consumed identically. The only new branch in it guards `randi() % winner_count` against drift's winner_count of 0. All placements of this token and of particle_randomness_evolutionary are bare, and apply_grid_config - a bare `pass` before this pass - takes only a word that validates AND differs, and never rebuilds anything.
dna.was: no exports of its own at all - a 12-line subclass whose whole body is `current_demo = 4; start_demo(4)`. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS and it was right about the file: every knob chapter five has belongs to its parent, extrem_randomness.gd, and the one that decides the artifact's subject - who counts as fit - was the literal 0.1 inside update_evolutionary_algorithms.

DO NOT DECLARE `chapter` ON THIS TOKEN: the export is real and the values are real, so the gate would pass it, but this subclass pins demo 4 in _ready AFTER super._ready() applies chapter - all six values would render the identical evolution demo and the sweep would publish six identical frames. The word `selection` is non_teleological_evolution's, and drift, uniform and split carry its meanings exactly. `runaway` is REFUSED: there it means the population standing at its own max_population ceiling with the field paved, and this population neither reproduces nor grows - it is a fixed 100 bodies - so runaway here could only be renamed to mean something else, which is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary. The two files also disagree about which value is home, and the disagreement is the honest content of the pair: drift is the default there because that artifact has no fitness function, and culled is the default here because this one has had one all along. CAVEAT FOR THE CRITIC: the optimum orbits on Time.get_ticks_msec(), which the wall clock at capture leaves at an arbitrary phase, so the cloud's POSITION varies between frames of one sweep. That was left alone rather than normalised, because normalising it would change what five live placements do. The axis signature is the gold count (0 / 10 / 100) and the cluster shape (2.5 m diffuse / 0.18 m knot / 1.9 m streak / two knots 2.50 m apart), all of which the Python re-implementation showed stable across four wall-clock phases. No `framing` hint is set: the title and description Label3D plates pull the union box wide and dilute the subject, but the swarm sits off-centre at x -5..0, and a tighter shot risks cropping drift's cloud while leaving culled's knot central - a difference manufactured by the camera. Measure first, then set it.

Five chapters existed in full in the file - each with its own opening arrangement in start_demo, its own update rule, its own colour law, its own title and its own paragraph of prose - and there was no way to stop on one, so every map that places this shows whichever page the ten-second clock happened to be on. Neither registry entry declares default_params and neither token carries a delegate, so merged_config is EMPTY at the three bare cells and GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` gate at :1194 means _apply_artifact_config is never called - no metadata is stamped and apply_grid_config is never reached. dna.was: Seventeen @exports - the richest export surface in the sequence - and not one of them said what the field is MADE of. generate_density_field is four lines of arithmetic: sample noise.get_noise_3d at the corner (:125), map it to (noise + 1) * 0.5 (:128), store. No shape term, no gradient, no bias, no second layer. So the picture is a level set of one FastNoiseLite object and nothing else - the sequence's purest case of a surface that is only a threshold on a field - and the two lines deciding what that object IS sat three apart as bare constants, TYPE_SIMPLEX at :63 and FRACTAL_FBM at :66, reachable from no map, no token and no inspector. apply_grid_config was the single word `pass` at :407: a config channel wired to nothing, so even the sixteen knobs that WERE exported could not be set by a placement.
dna.note: generator is SHARED, and the sharing is the whole point. FIVE artifacts already carry it with the same four values in the same order and the same default - perlin_noise (promoted 2026-07-29), noise_terrain (08-03), noise_space and shader_noise_space (08-05), alongside simplex_noise in the same bench family - and every one of their notes says the same sentence: the noise sequence is built on comparing bases, so if each artifact spells the comparison its own way there is nothing to compare. cellular, not worley, for the same reason. THE APPROVED DESIGN FOR THIS PASS PROPOSED A NEW WORD, `basis`, with five rungs (value|perlin|simplex|smooth|cells), and it was refused. A census of all 996 declared axes across the registry turned up `generator` on four tokens carrying exactly this value list; a sixth spelling of one question is precisely the fault those five notes were written to prevent. So: same word, same four rungs, same order, same default, `cells` spelled `cellular`, and `smooth` declined (see declined). What this member adds to the family is the READING and not the vocabulary - the other five displace a height or tint a wall with the basis, and this one level-sets it. Five artifacts asking one question and one of them asking it of a boundary instead of a surface is a comparison worth having; a sixth private word would have been six unrelated facts. ONE DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE, stated rather than glossed. The cellular rung here also sets cellular_return_type = RETURN_CELL_VALUE, which the other five do not. FastNoiseLite's default is RETURN_DISTANCE, distance-to-nearest-feature, whose one-point distribution is strongly one-sided. This file's iso_level is fixed at 0.5 and :128 maps noise to (n + 1) * 0.5, so 0.5 cuts the field exactly at its own mean - a threshold chosen for a zero-mean basis. Against a one-sided field that threshold stops being a mean, and the rung would mostly move HOW MUCH of the box is solid rather than what its boundary is made of. RETURN_CELL_VALUE is a constant per Voronoi cell with mean zero, so the cut stays at the mean and the answer is a surface with no curvature anywhere in the frame: flat plates meeting at cell walls. This is the same move shader_noise_space recorded when it amplitude-matched its four bases with three scaling constants so its axis would measure structure and not exposure. TerrainGenerator.gd:90 in this same repo already pairs TYPE_CELLULAR with RETURN_CELL_VALUE. accretion is NEW - zero uses among those 996 - and the adjacency is named rather than left for the critic. `octaves` is taken SEVEN times (mc_cave and mc_inside_cave in this sequence, plus noise_space, noise_quarry, simplex_noise, marchingcubes_cave, marchingcubes_inside_cave) and it counts HOW MANY scales survive. accretion is the RULE by which they are combined, and the count is held at this scene's shipped noise_octaves = 4 on every rung - deliberately untouched, though it is one of the seventeen exports - so the two questions cannot overlap. summed = FRACTAL_FBM SHIPPED. single = FRACTAL_NONE, one octave, the frame that shows what the other three rungs are adding. ridged = FRACTAL_RIDGED, which rectifies each octave to 1 - |n|; against simplex's mean |n| of about 0.35 that puts the field's mean near +0.3 instead of 0, so the cut at 0.5 leaves a sparser solid and the extracted surface grows blades and fins instead of lobes. pingpong = FRACTAL_PING_PONG at the engine's default fractal_ping_pong_strength of 2.0, folding the range repeatedly into banded shells and likewise skewing the mean positive. THE ARITHMETIC OF THE PICTURE, written down so a small number can be told from a dead axis. frequency is the .tscn's noise_scale 0.05, so the base wavelength is 20 world units across a 32-unit chunk: 1.6 periods per axis, i.e. the frame is dominated by one octave's worth of blob about 10 units across. Sampling is 32 points over 32 units, spacing 1.032, so the fourth octave at wavelength 2.5 is resolved at only 2.4 samples per period - right at Nyquist, and contributing at a gain of 0.125. That is why accretion is expected to be the quieter of the two axes, and it is a second reason the octave count was left alone. AND THE CAVEAT THE WHOLE FAMILY SHARES, which none of the five siblings has written down: at a fixed seed, changing noise_type does not perturb one field, it draws a different one. simplex and perlin at seed 1337 are two unrelated realisations, not two renderings of one landscape. A large bite on `generator` is therefore close to guaranteed whatever the design, and the thing to read is not the mean but the CHARACTER - whether value shows the axis-aligned creases of a cubic lattice, whether cellular shows flat plates. That is true of all five siblings equally, which is exactly what makes them comparable; it is a property of the axis and not a defect in it.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: perlin_noise, simplex_noise, noise_terrain, noise_space, shader_noise_space - `generator` is the same axis with the same four values in the same order and the same default. This is the sixth member and the first to level-set the field rather than displace a height or tint a wall with it, which is the reason to keep the word rather than coin one: if a shared vocabulary is honest, the odd member out is the interesting measurement. The single documented departure is cellular_return_type on the cellular rung, argued in `note`. `octaves`, which four of those five also carry, is NOT taken here - accretion asks a different question and the octave count is pinned so the two cannot be confused.
dna.declined: `smooth` (TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH), REFUSED, and it is the refusal that cost something. The approved design asked for it as a fifth rung and predicted it would be the weakest, closest to simplex at about 4% - 'only just over the bite floor'. It is dropped because the four-value list is a comparison instrument held in common by five artifacts, three of whose notes assert 'the same four values in the same order'; a fifth rung on one member makes that member's mean incomparable with the other four, and what it buys is the rung already predicted to be faintest. If the sweep later wants the simplex-versus-simplex-smooth distinction, it belongs to the whole family at once and not to this member alone. `basis`, REFUSED as a name - see note. num_points_per_axis (32) - the sampling resolution, and `resolution` is already this sequence's family word, held by animated_noise_explorer and by queer_marching_cave. Not taking it a third time. noise_scale (0.05) - the biggest knob by visual effect and the one this promotion was most tempted by. Refused because against a fixed 32-point lattice over a 32-unit chunk it is arithmetically the SAME ratio: chunk_size x noise_scale = 1.6 periods across the box, so halving the frequency is indistinguishable from doubling the lattice spacing. Sweeping it re-argues resolution from the other side. iso_level (0.5) - `threshold`, taken by mc_torus_sculpture. Recorded in the prose instead, because :128 maps the noise to (n + 1) * 0.5 and so 0.5 cuts the field exactly at its own mean, which is why the shipped picture is a balanced sponge with roughly equal solid and void - and why the cellular rung had to be mean-matched. noise_persistence (0.5) and noise_lacunarity (2.0) - genuine spectral properties, but both are octave-weighting parameters and would argue with accretion for the same pixels. noise_octaves (4) - `octaves`, taken seven times, and held fixed here precisely so accretion is not measured against it. glass_color, outline_color, outline_width, use_shader, generate_colliders, chunk_size - material, chrome and size. voxel_scale - exported since the file was written and read by nothing in the build path; a dead knob, not an axis, and deliberately kept out of the rebuild signature for that reason.

The subject is a cube-shaped, close to isotropic volume, so the fit-by-diagonal that letterboxes flat and thin subjects is honest here and no layers = 0 anchor is needed. THE ONE THING TO WATCH, because it is an inference and not a measurement: the density field is defined everywhere in the box at every rung, so every rung SHOULD reach every face - but ridged and pingpong push the field's mean positive and could in principle pull the surface in from the faces, which an AABB-fitted camera answers by zooming, turning a change of extent into a change of apparent scale. If the sweep shows two rungs framed at visibly different magnifications, that is the cause, and the fix is an anchor mesh rather than a smaller framing number.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was the single word `pass` at :407. It now reads the two axes against their allow-lists (an unrecognised value is DROPPED, not applied - the science_screen failure was a typo nothing in the chain refused) and rebuilds only when a signature of every value the build reads has actually moved. The signature is not a hand-listed tuple of the two axes: _signature() strings every export generate_world consumes, so the guard cannot drift out of step with the build. voxel_scale is deliberately absent from it - the export exists and nothing reads it, so including it would let a dead knob pay for a 29,791-cube re-march. The channel stays narrow on purpose: the two axes are the only keys READ, so a token naming noise_scale or iso_level still changes nothing, because widening the channel to honour keys nobody has ever sent would be a behaviour change hiding inside a promotion. ORDERING READ OFF THE CALL SITE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. GridInteractablesComponent stamps config_* metadata at :1656-1666 and calls add_child at :1220, so metadata always lands BEFORE _ready; _ready reads it through _read_dna_metadata and builds ONCE with the right values, records the signature, and the deferred apply_grid_config that follows finds the signature unchanged and returns. A `_built` flag guards the reverse order: config arriving before the first build assigns and returns, because _ready will read the new values on its way through. THE SCRIPTLESS ROOT IS NOT A FAULT AND WAS NOT 'FIXED'. The promotion brief called it a BLOCKING STRUCTURAL FAULT - voxel_noise_demo.tscn's root is a bare Node3D and VoxelNoiseMarchingCubes.gd sits on a child - and it asked for the script to be moved up. The engine was read instead of the brief, and the brief is stale. GridInteractablesComponent._apply_artifact_config falls through at :1695 to _config_holder, a breadth-first search for the first descendant that handles config, which finds the child, stamps the metadata there and calls apply_grid_config on it, all before add_child; capture_config_sweep._holder_of does the same per key for the bench; and check_dna_declarations.unreachable_roots classifies this shape as CHILD-ONLY, informational, explicitly not a fault, since e0bc97b3b. Moving the script would have been a change with a real cost and no benefit - the ROOT is where GridInteractablesComponent attaches its _RotationTimer, and this script's _exit_tree used to blanket-free every ownerless child, so the move would have newly put that timer inside the blast radius. The script therefore stayed put and the free was narrowed instead: an `_owned` array holds the two nodes this script creates (the VoxelWorld mesh and the VoxelWorldCollision body) and nothing else is ever touched, which is identical in effect today and stops being identical the moment anything attaches a helper here. clear_world also now DETACHES before queue_free, because queue_free is deferred and a rebuild adds a second node named VoxelWorld in the same frame, which Godot would silently rename to VoxelWorld2.
dna.still_note: A still is a complete account, and this is one of the few artifacts in the sequence where that needs no qualification. There is no _process, no timer, no await and no call_deferred anywhere in the file; _ready runs setup_noise, setup_marching_cubes_tables and generate_world synchronously and the mesh is finished when it returns. Both axes are resolved inside setup_noise before the first of 32,768 samples is taken and neither is re-read afterwards. Determinism is real rather than asserted: one FastNoiseLite, seeded from an export before first use, and no other source of randomness in the file. Four runs of the same rung are the same mesh. BUDGET, checked because the failure mode is a watchdog kill and not a bad picture: 32^3 = 32,768 noise samples and 31^3 = 29,791 marched cubes per tile, all in GDScript, with an Array-of-Triangle-objects intermediate. The registry's own compute field calls this artifact HEAVY. On a 16-tile sweep that is the number to watch against the 16-second stall rule, not the bite.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED BEFORE THE CAPTURE, and one of the two predictions deliberately DISAGREES with the approved design so the sweep can settle it - a prediction that agrees with the sweep is worth nothing. generator, closest pair: perlin x value, predicted ~30-35% of frame, i.e. nowhere near the bite floor, and the honest reading of that is that 'closest' barely means anything on this axis. Arithmetic: perlin and value sample the SAME cubic lattice at the same spacing (1 / 0.05 = 20 world units, 1.6 cells across the 32-unit chunk) and both are zero-mean, so both produce a sponge of the same characteristic blob size and roughly the same 50% solid fraction. They differ in placement, not in scale, and a pixel metric reads placement as large. cellular should be the loudest and the most obviously different - flat plates, no curvature. The part of this I am least sure of is whether `value` shows its axis-aligned creases at only 1.6 lattice cells per axis; if it does not, the value rung will read as one more unrelated sponge. accretion, closest pair: ridged x pingpong, predicted ~12% of frame. THE APPROVED DESIGN PREDICTED summed x pingpong AT ~8% AND THIS PASS DISAGREES WITH IT. Arithmetic: ridged and pingpong both rectify or fold each octave into a one-sided shape, so both fields carry a mean around +0.3 to +0.5 against summed's 0.0; after density = (n + 1) * 0.5 and the cut at 0.5, both leave a sparse thin-walled solid of roughly a quarter to a third of the volume, while summed and single both leave a balanced sponge at about a half. If the family splits that way, the design's pair is wrong and the axis is really asking 'is the octave rectified'. If summed x pingpong really is the closest, the folding is being re-sorted back into a balanced sponge by the threshold and the axis is asking 'how many scales', which would put it too close to `octaves` to keep - so this pair decides whether accretion earns its own word. Largest pair, both predictions agreeing: single x ridged. THE DEGENERACY RISK WORTH NAMING: if ridged or pingpong pushes the mean far enough that almost every corner lands on one side of 0.5, march_cube skips the cube as 'completely inside or outside' (:205) and the tile comes back near-empty - which reads exactly like an inert axis. Read the per-tile triangle count that generate_world prints at :106 BEFORE reading the bite number.

dna.was: no exports on the root at all - the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The two decisions that carry the argument sat one node down as constants: which basis fills the field, and whether a sample is read as elevation or as measurement. Note that the artifact called Perlin Noise has been drawing SIMPLEX noise since it was written; the promotion makes that a declared choice (generator=perlin is now available) rather than silently correcting it and rewriting seven maps.

perlin_noise.description: Interactive Perlin noise generation and visualization
perlin_noise.name: Perlin Noise
perlin_noise.qfep_connection: Perlin's gift to graphics: gradients on a lattice, interpolated smoothly — randomness that flows instead of stutters. Every organic-looking surface in games descends from this trick. The demo hands you the dials: octaves stacking detail, persistence deciding how loudly the small scales speak.

perlin_noise_clouds.description: Interactive 3D volumetric cloud generation using Perlin noise for atmospheric and procedural sky effects
perlin_noise_clouds.name: Perlin Noise Clouds
perlin_noise_clouds.qfep_connection: The cloud negotiates its own density against an 11-millisecond frame budget, shedding particles whenever 90 fps is threatened. What reads as weather is a scheduler deciding how much sky you can afford — atmosphere as a performance contract.

perlin_noise_terrain.description: Interactive 3D terrain generation using Perlin noise algorithms
perlin_noise_terrain.name: Perlin Noise Terrain
perlin_noise_terrain.qfep_connection: The Perlin pipeline run to its natural end: octaves become mountain ranges, persistence becomes ruggedness. Parameter names turn geological — the chapter's clearest case of mathematics wearing the world's clothes.

perlinvolume.description: 3D Perlin noise volume generation for procedural content creation and spatial algorithms
perlinvolume.name: Perlin Volume
perlinvolume.qfep_connection: All the work happens in the shader's ray march; the script only spins the box. Noise here is not scattered points but a solid you can look into — coherence as a volume, resampled by every ray.

dna.default: rule=trail - trail is the fall-through arm of the match in _choose_next_position and reproduces the shipped law line for line: the same eight compass directions in the order they were always built, the same seed value best_pheromone = -1.0, a STRICT > so ties fall to the first entry (which on blank ground means Right, and that quirk is preserved deliberately), the same bounds test, the same single randf() before it and the same randi() modulo n on the random arm. The random STREAM is unchanged too: _create_walkers still takes exactly two draws per walker in the same order, and the heading added to the walker dictionary is assigned from COMPASS by INDEX rather than drawn. walk_seed defaults to -1, which routes every draw back to the global unseeded generator exactly as today, and warmup_steps defaults to 0, which returns before touching anything. apply_grid_config was literally `pass` and is now an ASSIGNMENT-ONLY body that rebuilds nothing - it arrives through call_deferred, so it lands after _ready has built the grids, and a rebuild would wipe a terrain the room has been growing since the player walked in. All 3 placements (Random_Pheromone, Room_Random_Pheromone, Corridor_Random_Pheromone) carry the bare token with no config keys at all, so not one branch of it is reachable from any map that exists.
dna.was: no axis, and no way in at all: apply_grid_config was a one-line `pass`, so the fourteen @exports were unreachable from a map token and the runner refused the artifact for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. That was literally true here in a way it was not for most of the batch. The walker's decision law - eight directions, argmax pheromone at sensor_distance, otherwise random - was welded into _choose_next_position with the direction list rebuilt inline on every call, and the only thing the scene could argue with was how MUCH the walkers follow (pheromone_attraction, and only by editing the .tscn), never WHAT following means.
dna.shared_with: `rule` is mold_network's word for exactly this slot - the transition law - seconded by structure_growth, complexity_pattern and lifeform_walker, and it is taken deliberately rather than invented. THE VALUE LIST IS NOT SHARED AND CANNOT BE, for the same reason mold_network gives for not sharing with the Life family: those are survive/born bands over a cell's neighbours and this is one walker choosing one of eight compass steps, a different alphabet in which '4-6/5-7' means nothing. These should NOT be compared as a family measurement. The word carries; the numbers must not.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. THE RULE IS VISIBLE IN A STILL AND THE RATE IS NOT, which is the whole reason this is the axis. deposit-per-step, decay-per-second and steps-per-second are the knobs a reader reaches for first and every one of them is a fact about time that a single frame cannot hold; what a frame CAN hold is the shape the ground ended up in. Each value changes one clause of the same decision and nothing else - which neighbours are candidates, or the sign of the comparison. trail is self-reinforcing and converges: the walkers commit to paths they made and the plot grows a few thick ridges. sniff gives the walker a heading and only the three steps in front of it, so it cannot double back into its own trail and the same attraction lays long smooth arcs instead of knots - the Physarum reading, in which the body remembers as well as the environment. avoid flips the sign and flees the strongest scent, so no ridge ever forms and the plot churns evenly - the anti-stigmergy case the artifact's own @identity names when it says it contrasts with pixel_cloud. grid narrows the candidates to the four cardinal neighbours, and the lattice stops being a substrate and becomes the result: right-angled ridges, a street plan rather than a delta. TWO THINGS THE SHIPPED CODE DID NOT SURVIVE UNPATCHED, both found by reading rather than by running: the border branch of _walk_step `continue`s WITHOUT choosing a direction, so a heading-locked walker would push at the same wall for ever - the heading is reversed there, which costs no random draw and is inert under the other three values; and _forward_cone returns STRAIGHT ON first, because the shipped law breaks ties on the first entry and on unwalked ground every candidate senses 0.0, so a turn at index 0 would fill the plot with same-handed spirals and publish a fact about list order as a fact about stigmergy.
dna.fixture_note: two knobs, both new, both defaulting to shipped behaviour so neither is an axis, and both necessary before any frame of this artifact means anything. walk_seed pins the walk: it defaults to -1, which routes every draw to the global unseeded generator exactly as the shipped code did, and without it four rule variants are four different landscapes and the sweep measures the RNG - the brief's 'confident bite on a generative artifact' row. warmup_steps makes the frame a KNOWN AGE. This is the harder of the two: _process only rebuilds the mesh on a step, walk_speed is 5 so a step is 0.2 s, and the capture settles for 1.1 s - so the shipped artifact photographs as a FLAT PLANE with five or six vertices nudged, under every value, and the axis would have read INERT as a fact about the bench. 400 steps decayed at the real 0.2 s interval is the shipped dynamics played fast rather than a different process; at raise_amount 0.2 that is 1600 vertex raises on a 60 x 60 interior, enough for ridges of a metre or more on a 20 m plate. It costs about 2.6 M grid touches inside _ready, which is a fraction of a second and well inside the watchdog's grace, but it is the number to lower first if a boot stalls.
dna.still_note: framing 0.65, derived: the plate is 20 x 20 m so the box radius is about 14.1 m, the no-crop floor is 1/PAD = 0.526, and 0.65 opens the frame to roughly 34.8 m across - the plate at about 57 percent of frame width with 23 percent margin on the corners, against 37 percent at framing 1.0. THE COLOUR SURVIVES, which was checked rather than assumed: the scene's material is the SimpleGrid wireframe shader, not a StandardMaterial3D, so the vertex_color_use_as_albedo line in _ready never fires - but the shader reads COLOR into instanceColor and, because modelColor is grey rather than white, takes the instance colour whenever it is not white. _update_mesh writes Color.WHITE.lerp(pheromone_color, intensity), so unwalked ground stays grey and fresh trail reads magenta. So the frame carries the argument twice over: the HEIGHT is the permanent record and the MAGENTA is the short-term one (a cell decays from 0.6 to 0 in fifteen steps), and the two say different things about the same rule. The camera sits 15 degrees above the horizon, which foreshortens a flat plate but shows relief against the horizon, so ridge SHAPE reads better than ridge position. NOT MEASURED - no capture was run in this pass and this arithmetic is the evidence offered in its place.
dna.declined: pheromone_attraction is NOT an axis, although the artifact's own @identity nominates it as the critical_parameter. It is a continuous dial between the shipped law and a pure random walk, it is now config-reachable through apply_grid_config like every other numeric export, and naming a value `wander` for attraction = 0 would be a second word for a knob that exists - projection_shadow's test. That is also why the value list has no null anchor: the null of this axis is a number, and it is already spelled. Nothing in the deposit / decay / speed group was considered for longer than it took to remember that a still cannot see a rate.

pheromone_terrain.description: Swarm-based terrain generation where agents deposit pheromone trails that shape the landscape. Demonstrates emergent self-organization from simple local rules.
pheromone_terrain.name: Pheromone Terrain

pickup_cube_placer.description: Finds the active grid system and populates pickup cubes using randomized or patterned placement modes.
pickup_cube_placer.name: pickup_cube_placer

pipe_dream.description: A 3D recreation of the classic Windows Pipes screensaver. Grows a colored pipe that randomly changes direction, building an intricate network over 100 segments.
pipe_dream.name: Pipe Dream
pipe_dream.qfep_connection: The Windows Pipes screensaver reborn: a pipe growing by random turns, filling the volume with plumbing nobody designed. Idle-machine art — the desktop's oldest proof that a few dice and a growth rule can furnish a world.

dna.fixture_why: BOTH ENTRIES ARE MANDATORY and neither is an axis. walk_seed: the run is nothing but accumulated draws from an rng that _ready calls randomize() on, so five unseeded frames are five different pipes and any bite number would be measuring the generator rather than the rung — the generative-artifact trap in CLAUDE.md. -1 is the default and keeps randomize(), so no placement sees the pin. growth: the shipped walk lays one length every 0.08 s, i.e. 14.4 s for the full 180. The sweep settles 1.1 s (about thirteen lengths) and its fixed-camera AABB pre-pass settles 0.35 s (about four), which is why this artifact's measured aabb_size in this very file is [0.24, 0.24, 0.95] — the size of ONE segment. Without the pin the sheet would compare five pictures of a stub and the camera would be framed for a stub. `instant` lays the whole run inside _ready; `live` is the default and is the shipped screensaver. It is a String enum and not a bool because the sweep sets exports from JSON before _ready and a typed bool silently rejects a fixture string.
dna.default: residue=path - the shipped drawing, in the shipped order. At `path` the rung is 2, _create_next_segment calls exactly the two functions it always called (_add_segment then _add_joint), and none of _mark_head, _trim_tail, _refresh_rails or _build_ghosts is reached; the only work this promotion adds on that path is one append to a PackedVector3Array and one dictionary lookup per length. The turn rule was refactored to take its generator and position as arguments so the ensemble's counterfactuals can call the same function, and the draw order is unchanged: one randf() for the straight-ahead check, then one randi_range per shuffle swap, exactly as before. _add_segment now derives its basis from the span end-start rather than from the `direction` member, which is the identical vector at that point by construction. MEASURED, not assumed: 6 mentions across 5 map files - bare tokens in Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness, Room_Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness and Random_Rotate_Random_Y, `pipe_dream:0:5` and `pipe_dream:0:8` in Corridor_Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness (rotation and y-offset, which the grid consumes, not this artifact), and membership in two curation_station collections in Curation_Bay_randomness_7 and Corridor_Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness whose #layout and #with_* keys belong to the station. Not one of them carries a residue key, and apply_grid_config returns on its second line unless a token names this axis.
dna.was: eleven exports and not one of them turnable: pipe_radius, segment_length, max_segments, bounds_extent, turn_interval, continue_straight_chance, growth_tween_time and five colour and energy fields - how BIG and how FAST, never what the cube is left holding. apply_grid_config was a literal `pass`, so none of the eleven was reachable from a map token even as a number. The runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS on exactly that ground.
dna.note: The word is the group's, taken with its answers rather than borrowed as a label: head < tail < path < envelope < ensemble, the same five in the same order and the same meaning as random_walk_128, random_walk_leash and random_walk_collection. The one place this member differs is worth stating plainly - THE WINDOW AT `tail` IS CUT IN TIME here, not in space. The three siblings draw on pages and keep pixels, so `recently` had to be approximated by a disc around the walker; this record is a list of turns in the order they were taken, so the window is the real thing. The rungs stay strictly nested either way, so no rung invents pipe the run did not lay. `envelope` is the rung this artifact answers best and is why the word fits at all: the desire line says the pipe explores a sealed cube until the cube is full, bounds_extent is the cube it was ALLOWED, and the rails are the cube it USED - never the same box, and the tangle alone cannot say which.
dna.declined: joint - the turn rule (ball / bare / collar), and the strongest other candidate in the file. The sphere at each corner is what makes 180 loose cylinders read as continuous plumbing, and removing it reveals the pipe as sticks that merely overlap, which is a genuine argument about the object. It is declined for a CAMERA reason and not a design one: a corner is 0.34 m on an object whose fitted box is about 13 m across, so at the sweep's fit-by-diagonal framing four values would differ by a handful of pixels - the line_interface fault. It wants its own pass at dna.framing near 0.3 and cannot share a sheet with an axis whose whole subject is the extent of the tangle. Also declined: continue_straight_chance, the file's former declared critical_parameter, because inertia changes how much tangle there is and not what the tangle claims (the reason rhizomatic_maze_space declined its six growth floats); and turn_interval and growth_tween_time, which are rates and invisible to a still.
dna.finding: THE @identity WAS WRONG ABOUT THE ALGORITHM and the header is corrected in this pass rather than papered over. It called this `a self-avoiding 3D random walk ... never crossing itself`. It is not, and never was: _choose_next_direction refuses only the reverse direction and any step that would leave bounds_extent, there is no occupancy set anywhere in the file, and the run crosses itself freely. Making it genuinely self-avoiding would be a different artifact and a change to all five existing placements, so it is not done here.
dna.still_note: residue is resolved before each length is laid and the rungs differ in how much geometry exists, so one frame is a complete account. Expect head-vs-path to be the loudest pair by a distance - one 0.5 m sphere against a 13 m tangle is a silhouette, not a texture. envelope-vs-path is the pair to check second and the one most likely to read small: twelve rails at 0.034 m radius on a 13 m box is thin ink, so if it comes back under 1% compare the silhouettes before believing it. ensemble triples the ink inside the same cube and should be unmistakable.

dna.default: bias=rise, evidence=result - the shipped build exactly: +Y weighted by upward_bias (3.0) and every other direction 1.0, one randf() per step in the same order, the path cubes and nothing beside them. walk_seed defaults to -1, which draws from the global stream as before, so the 8 existing placements keep rolling a fresh sculpture per launch; the fixture above is for the sweep only.
dna.was: grid_size, num_cubes, cube_spacing and upward_bias were @exports that apply_grid_config ignored (its body was `pass`), so no map token could reach the pull the @identity block names as the critical parameter; the refusals that shape a self-avoiding walk were discarded at build time and only the surviving path was ever shown.

pixel_cloud.description: Builds an upward-biased self-avoiding random walk and places cubes along the path to form a pixel cloud sculpture.
pixel_cloud.name: pixel_cloud

plane_manipulator.description: This script animates a random walk on a 3D plane. It simulates walkers that move across the plane's surface, raising the ground to create trails in real-time.
plane_manipulator.name: plane_manipulator
plane_manipulator.qfep_connection: The walk is not drawn on the surface; it becomes the surface. Each walker raises the ground it crosses into a trail, and the untouched border is the only place the plane remembers being flat.

plane_random.description: Generates a planar surface with random vertex displacement, creating organic undulating terrain from flat geometry.
plane_random.name: Plane Random
plane_random.qfep_connection: One vertex per second, plus or minus half a meter, forever: terrain here is not designed but accrued, and the heightmap collider keeps pace so your feet ratify each coin flip as ground.

pollock_3d.description: Interactive 3D Jackson Pollock-inspired art using movement-based procedural randomness
pollock_3d.name: Pollock 3D
pollock_3d.qfep_connection: Pollock minus the body: a Timer fires every half second and gesture is a curve through random points with viscosity presets named Thin, Medium, Thick. The drip is simulated; the risk — an arm that could miss — is not, and max_splats = 5000 is the conservation policy the real canvas never signed.

dna.default: support=floor - the shipped staging to the two numbers: rotation_degrees (-90, 180, 0) at y = floor_height (0.02), the same escape hatch when place_on_floor is false, and the frame and backing panels built off that same transform. The 3 existing placements pass no support key, so apply_grid_config returns on its first line and nothing restages.
dna.was: the canvas was hard-coded flat on the ground. Pollock's break was not a mark but a POSTURE - the canvas came off the easel and went on the studio floor, and the body walked around a thing it could no longer face - and this artifact shipped that decision as an un-turnable boolean. The axis restores the ladder the drip argued against: the floor stood over, the table leaned across, the easel it was supposed to sit at, the wall the finished picture ends up on. The word `support` is the art-historical term for the thing a painting is made on; the value list is NOT the one code_display and catalyst_target use for the same word, because theirs asks what furniture holds an instrument up and this asks which posture the body has to take.

pollock_painting_in_3d.description: Interactive 3D Jackson Pollock-inspired painting using movement-based procedural randomness
pollock_painting_in_3d.name: Pollock Painting in 3D

pool_hole_noise.description: Interactive cellular noise generation with pool hole pattern visualization
pool_hole_noise.name: Pool Hole Noise
pool_hole_noise.qfep_connection: Pools eat the terrain on a half-second growth timer while the shader hands out identity by altitude alone — below one threshold you are deep water, above another you are shore. Classification by height cut: the ground has no kinds, only elevations that get read as kinds.

prng_crank_machine.description: A physical pseudo-random number generator machine. Press CRANK to step the LCG formula: state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32. Each step animates multiply, add, mod phases. Shows deterministic sequence, normalized 0-1 output, and full history.
prng_crank_machine.name: PRNG Crank Machine
prng_crank_machine.qfep_connection: Determinism masquerading as randomness — structure hidden in apparent chaos.

probability_distributions_3d.description: Interactive 3D visualization of various probability distributions and statistical patterns
probability_distributions_3d.name: Probability Distributions 3D

random_bell_curve.description: Builds a 20x20 quad grid shaped into a 3D Gaussian bell curve with HeightMapShape3D collisions. Optional surface noise adds organic variation.
random_bell_curve.name: Random Bell Curve Terrain
random_bell_curve.qfep_connection: The bell made object: samples piling into the curve that chance keeps its accounts in. No single draw knows about the bell; the bell knows about all of them.

dna.default: arrival=scatter - the shipped path exactly: butterflies spawn at uniformly random points in the wander volume with white wings and nothing is staged. The spawner only calls stage_arrival() when arrival is NOT scatter, so all 10 existing placements (Museum_Wings, Random_Entropy, the three Spaceform rooms, the Random_Definition family, Corridor_randomness, Curation_Bay_randomness_4, Furnished_CAP_1, TemplateMap_Descent13) render byte-identically to before.
dna.was: three exports, all budget - butterfly_scene, spawn_interval, max_butterflies. Nothing the artifact argued was settable, so the swarm had only ever been found mid-wander.
dna.argues: a random walker in a room with an entropy gradient is not uniformly distributed. scatter shows the process (chance looking like chance), landed shows the result (the distribution collapsed onto the attractor), gathering shows both at once as direction rather than position.
dna.fixture_note: shipped behaviour spawns ONE butterfly at _ready and one more every 10s, so a 0.35s still holds a single speck and no arrival value is distinguishable from another - a distribution of one sample is not a distribution. swarm_seed pins the whole swarm so the three variants are the same eight butterflies photographed at three moments, not three different swarms. Both stay at their shipped defaults (1 and 0) outside the bench.
dna.declined: a second axis on what the wing tint ENCODES. Under the default arrival=scatter the wings are white - tinting only accumulates while sitting - so a tint axis swept from defaults would measure inert, and pinning arrival=landed in the fixture is impossible while arrival is itself the axis. Also declined: spawn_interval, entropy_seek_chance, wing_tint_speed. Every one is a rate and a rate cannot be photographed.

random_butterflies.description: Entropy-seeking butterfly swarm: wander randomly then land on entropy_axiom grid points, wings tinting blue-to-red along the order-chaos gradient. Grab and release to send to a new entropy point.
random_butterflies.name: Random Butterflies
random_butterflies.qfep_connection: Butterflies scattered by draw — position, wing-beat, drift all sampled. The prettiest argument in the room that entropy is freedom: nothing places them, and that is why they look alive.

random_color_book_page_collection.description: Interactive collection of randomly generated colored book pages using procedural algorithms
random_color_book_page_collection.name: Random Color Book Page Collection
random_color_book_page_collection.qfep_connection: The RAND million-random-digits book re-typeset in color: indexed rows, a side number scaled from the 1955 original, every swatch a fresh randf() — staging the bureaucratic labor it once took to publish disorder as a reference work.

random_decay_multimesh.description: Two standing 2D decay stacks rendered with MultiMesh: 1m cubes and 1dm prisms that gradually drift, rotate, sink, and darken.
random_decay_multimesh.name: Random Decay MultiMesh

random_decay_objects.description: Interactive visualization of random decay processes and object degradation
random_decay_objects.name: Random Decay Objects
random_decay_objects.qfep_connection: Decay runs only while your hand closes on the paper: each frame one random prism in the 9×9 grid picks up a millimetre of drift and a degree of tilt. Entropy staged as consent — release the grab and the ruin pauses mid-sentence.

random_edge_profile.description: A planar surface that generates random edge profiles and patterns
random_edge_profile.name: Random Edge Profile
random_edge_profile.qfep_connection: Chance under clamped boundary conditions: the heights are pure RNG draws, but the profile is forced to start and end at 0.5. Randomness admitted only in the interior; the frame stays negotiated.

random_edge_profile_collection.description: Interactive collection of random edge profiles for procedural geometry generation
random_edge_profile_collection.name: Random Edge Profile Collection
random_edge_profile_collection.qfep_connection: Only the top edge is allowed to be random; every other vertex of the plane keeps its factory coordinates. A profile is a managed frontier — noise granted to the silhouette, denied to the body it outlines.

random_gaussian_texture.description: Interactive Gaussian distribution texture generation for natural random patterns
random_gaussian_texture.name: Random Gaussian Texture
random_gaussian_texture.qfep_connection: Each dot lands at alpha 0.004 — individually almost nothing — so the bell curve exists only as accumulation. The Gaussian is a crowd phenomenon: a law legible in aggregate and deniable in every single event.

random_number_book_page_1955.description: A single page from the RAND Corporation 1955 random digit table. Numbers cascade live top-to-bottom. Touch any 5-digit number to freeze it in amber — the rest keep flowing.
random_number_book_page_1955.name: Random Number Book Page 1955
random_number_book_page_1955.qfep_connection: A page from A Million Random Digits (RAND, 1955) — the book nobody reads and everybody trusted. Before hardware entropy, randomness was a print run: tables harvested from an electronic roulette, proofread for bias, sold to scientists who needed disorder they could cite. Chance with an ISBN — the moment entropy became infrastructure.

random_number_book_page_collection.description: RAND Corporation 1955 random digit table brought to life. Numbers cascade top-to-bottom like a stock ticker. Touch any number in VR to freeze it — frozen numbers glow amber while the rest keep flowing. Demonstrates that randomness is a process, not a snapshot.
random_number_book_page_collection.name: Random Number Book — Live Cascade
random_number_book_page_collection.qfep_connection: Randomness as flow — freezing a number is an act of observation that collapses possibility into fixed value.

random_plants.description: Interactive procedural plant generation with random growth patterns and organic forms
random_plants.name: Random Plants
random_plants.qfep_connection: A hundred draws against four probability sliders sort the world into tree, bush, flower, grass: variety as budget allocation, the taxonomy fixed before the first trunk is placed.

random_transformations.description: Interactive visualization of random geometric transformations and spatial manipulations
random_transformations.name: Random Transformations
random_transformations.qfep_connection: Every frame the originals and their transformed doubles are queue_freed and redrawn, so no random draw persists long enough to become a history. Variance in rotation, scale, and translation is the advertised subject; the deeper randomness on display is the refusal of duration.

random_transformations_geometric.name: Random Transformations - Geometric
random_transformations_geometric.qfep_connection: Geometry under dice: translate, rotate, scale, each parameter drawn. The form survives as a family resemblance across its own variations — identity loosened, not lost. Entropy applied to shape is variation; applied without bound, dissolution.

random_transformations_matrices.name: Random Transformations - Matrices
random_transformations_matrices.qfep_connection: A 4×4 matrix laid out as floor boxes, green rising for positive entries, red for negative — while the 'determinant' sphere overhead pulses on sin(time), wired to nothing in the matrix below. The summary scalar is decoration; only the raw entries are telling the truth.

random_transformations_noise.name: Random Transformations - Noise
random_transformations_noise.qfep_connection: Sixty times a second the whole 8×8 grid is deleted and regrown, each cube colored by how far the noise field threw it from its station. Deviation worn as hue — the most visible property of every object is its distance from where it was assigned to stand.

random_transformations_stochastic.name: Random Transformations - Stochastic
random_transformations_stochastic.qfep_connection: Four vocabularies of chance stand in parallel columns — uniform, Gaussian, exponential, Poisson — twenty fresh samples each, every frame. The distributions are compared not by formula but by posture: how each cloud of spheres carries its spread.

random_walk_128.description: Fine-grained random walk on 128x128 grid using tiny cubes
random_walk_128.name: Random Walk 128x128
random_walk_128.qfep_connection: A walk at 128x128 grain: one wanderer, tiny steps, no memory. The fine grid turns the walk's statistics visible — dense scribble near the origin, thinning frontier — chance accumulating into a shape no single step intended.

random_walk_collection.description: Interactive paper that demonstrates random walk algorithms with grab and manipulation capabilities
random_walk_collection.name: Random Walk Grab Paper
random_walk_collection.qfep_connection: Many walks released together: each path senseless alone, the ensemble growing the square-root halo the mathematics promised. The collection is the lesson — randomness has laws, but only in the plural.

random_walk_grab_paper.description: Interactive paper that demonstrates random walk algorithms with grab and manipulation capabilities
random_walk_grab_paper.name: Random Walk Grab Paper
random_walk_grab_paper.qfep_connection: The walk advances only while the paper is in your hand; set it down and the trace halts mid-drift. Which of seven walk grammars you are holding was itself drawn at random at startup — you read the trail to learn what kind of chance you've been carrying.

random_walk_leash.description: A glowing orb on a leash that tugs in random directions. Grab it in VR and feel the random walk through your hand. The orb pulses with each impulse. A trail traces the walk path. Stats track drift vs sqrt(N) theoretical scaling.
random_walk_leash.name: Random Walk Leash
random_walk_leash.qfep_connection: Embodied randomness — the walk isn't watched, it's felt. Your arm becomes the accumulator of stochastic impulses.

randomize_cubes_over_Z.description: Distributes cubes with increasing randomness along the Z-axis, visualizing a gradient from order to disorder.
randomize_cubes_over_Z.name: Randomize Cubes Over Z
randomize_cubes_over_Z.qfep_connection: Disorder is rationed by coordinate: jitter, tilt, and scale all multiply by z², so the front rank stands at attention while the back rows blur. A walkable gradient from F_order to E_flux — and the squaring means order holds far deeper into the room than the eye predicts.

randomlines.description: ImmediateMesh random line segments with 3 distributions (uniform/Gaussian/clustered), 3 color modes (solid/golden-ratio/length-gradient), optional drift animation and bounding box. Config: num_lines, area_size_x/y/z, distribution, cluster_count, cluster_spread, color_mode, animate, drift_speed, show_bounding_box
randomlines.name: Random Lines
randomlines.qfep_connection: A line is just two samples from a distribution, and the color mode confesses the statistics: short segments green, long ones red. Swap uniform for clustered and the same forty lines become a different society — geometry as the visible residue of a sampling law.

randompoint.description: Drops a single draggable point inside an XY bounds and keeps its billboarded coordinate label in range.
randompoint.name: randompoint

randompoints.capacity: DISTINGUISH structured randomness from uniform randomness by seeing how a single constraint (minimum distance) transforms a point cloud from chaos to jazz
randompoints.description: Three distributions reveal three relationships with space. Uniform scatters without memory — each point ignores every other. Gaussian clusters around a center — proximity is destiny. Blue noise enforces minimum distance via dart-throwing rejection, structured randomness where emptiness is forbidden. The critical parameter is blue_noise_min_dist: the exclusion radius that converts white noise into jazz. Contrasts with randompoint (single white noise); prepares for Perlin noise (structured randomness with continuity).
interactions: observe packing limit in blue noise mode
randompoints.name: randompoints

parameters.blue_noise_min_dist: Minimum distance for blue noise rejection (default: 0.25)

randompoints.qfep_connection: Pure E(S) — three distributions at three lambda values. Uniform is maximum entropy (lambda=0). Gaussian introduces spatial bias (lambda rising). Blue noise enforces a minimum-distance constraint that converts raw entropy into structured randomness — lambda at full strength, where constraint produces beauty, not order.

randompoints_gaussian.description: Variant of the grab-point scatter preconfigured to sample from a 3D Gaussian cloud with labeled spheres.
randompoints_gaussian.name: randompoints_gaussian

randompoints_uniform.description: Scatters grab spheres uniformly through a bounding box and labels each point.
randompoints_uniform.name: randompoints_uniform
randompoints_uniform.qfep_connection: Thirty labeled grab spheres flung through a box by randf_range: uniformity you can walk into and refute by hand, because clusters and voids appear that no biased process made. Even-handedness does not look even — that scandal is the lesson.

randomup.description: Randomly elevates objects upward with varying heights, demonstrating basic vertical displacement using uniform randomness.
randomup.name: Random Up
randomup.qfep_connection: A coin weighted 60-40 toward heaven builds the palace: each upward win lays a three-metre slope cube so the climb stays walkable, and a nav graph records every wager. Architecture as accumulated bias — the building is the histogram of its own coin flips.

rejection_sampling_demo.description: Visual scatter plot of the accept/reject method for sampling arbitrary distributions. 2000 uniform random points plotted against a Gaussian target curve — green dots accepted (below curve), red dots rejected (above). Shows acceptance ratio.
rejection_sampling_demo.name: Rejection Sampling Demo

dna.host_note: aabb_size [0,0,0] - this artifact IS an operation on the host map grid, not an object. It hunts a MultiMeshInstance3D through get_parent() and rewrites its transforms, so standalone there is nothing to remove and nothing to photograph; the loop declined it for having no body. The sweep now builds the grid it is looking for.

remove_random.description: A demolition algorithm that randomly removes cubes from the grid
remove_random.name: Random Destructor
remove_random.qfep_connection: The demolition primitive: cubes deleted by chance, the grid thinned by dice. Where every other builder in this world adds, this one subtracts without a plan — and the room that remains is a negative sculpture of the sequence of draws. Entropy as an editor.

rotate_grid_cubes.description: A grid of cubes rotated in repeating row-based patterns. The lattice stays fixed while orientation changes propagate across it, making the difference between flat and tilted sections immediately readable. Animation exposes rotation as a patterned field rather than a single isolated action. It shows how a transformation can be distributed across a structure.
rotate_grid_cubes.name: Rotate Grid Cubes

dna.default: score=bands, grain=rows - bands returns the untouched const PATTERN (6 Z / 4 flat / 6 Y / 4 flat / 6 X-neg / 4 flat / 6 all / 8 flat) and rows returns the int(round(pos.z)) index this file has always used, so all 6 placements render byte-for-byte as before; apply_grid_config now re-applies only when a value actually moved, so a map that passes no keys keeps exactly what _ready built
dna.was: one hard-coded const PATTERN of (row_count, axis) bands, indexed by the cube's z row. Only the DEGREES were exposed (rot_amount, rot_amount_y) - which is the least interesting thing about it. The @identity block already named the band list the critical_parameter and the code kept it const.

It hunts a MultiMeshInstance3D through its `../GridMultiMesh` NodePath and rewrites the host grid's transforms - the same class as Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ and remove_random, which is why the runner first read it as having nothing to photograph. 26 rows deep shows the first three bands of the 44-row cycle mirrored about the centre; 16 wide keeps grain=columns and grain=rings legible.
dna.fixture_note: use_animation false so the still photographs the settled tilt rather than a frame of the 1 s tween.

rotate_grid_cubes.qfep_connection: Transformation modifies orientation across S while the grid itself remains stable. Patterned rotation makes state change legible as repetition and variation on a fixed lattice.
rotate_grid_cubes.capacity: READ patterned rotation across a fixed lattice and compare flat rows against tilted ones.
interactions: watch the rotation pattern move across rows
change rot_amount and rot_amount_y to reshape the pattern
compare flat sections with rotated ramps or slopes

rotate_random_y.description: Applies random Y-axis rotation to objects, creating varied orientations while maintaining vertical alignment.
rotate_random_y.name: Rotate Random Y
rotate_random_y.qfep_connection: One pass at load: every instanced cube nudged around Y by a random fraction of a degree, then left alone forever. The imperceptible wobble is what keeps the MultiMesh from confessing itself — sameness needs a pinch of noise to read as world rather than copy.

sculpt_one.description: An artistic sculpting algorithm that randomly modifies and shapes geometric forms
sculpt_one.name: Sculpt One
sculpt_one.qfep_connection: Sculpting by random modification: a form shaped by accepting the dice's suggestions. The sculptor keeps only the veto — chance proposes every stroke. Authorship as curation of accidents.

dna.default: hand=composition, substance=mixed - the three existing placements are untouched: `composition` runs the same five sculpting moves in the same order create_composition() always ran them, and `substance` returns from _apply_substance() before touching a single material, leaving the curated palette exactly as create_materials() built it.
dna.was: One still-life with no knobs. Five sculpting moves ran unconditionally and the piece was their sum; the palette was eight hand-typed materials. The @identity had asked for a palette dial, a reseed and a gloss-to-fabric slider as [missing] since the file was written.
dna.note: `hand` is maze_generation's word — which procedure makes the form — with this artifact's own moves as its rungs. `substance` is rainbow's word — what the thing is made of — with a rung list this piece can actually be: a still-life of cloth and liquid has no 'light'. Colour is held constant across substance, so the axis is a claim about surface and nothing else. sculpt_seed defaults to 0 = unseeded, which is the shipped behaviour (a fresh composition every launch); the fixture pins it so a sweep photographs ONE object under two axes instead of nine different objects. AXIS ORDER IS DELIBERATE: build_dna_gallery trims the SECOND axis to fit the 9-frame cap, so substance leads with all four rungs and hand contributes composition|pour — 4x2=8 frames covering both — rather than hand taking all five and leaving substance unmeasured.

shader_07_noise.description: Book of Shaders chapter 7 — value noise, gradient noise, simplex noise implemented as GPU shaders on a quad display.
shader_07_noise.name: Shader Noise Functions

shader_08_cellularnoise.description: Book of Shaders chapter 8 — Voronoi and Worley noise patterns rendered as GPU shaders. Shows distance fields and cell boundaries.
shader_08_cellularnoise.name: Cellular Noise Shader

dna.fixture_why: Every visible parameter of this room is driven off a clock in _process — time, time_scale, cloud_density and both colours all move — so a still is taken at whatever instant the shutter happened to fall. `frozen` leaves the .tscn's own authored uniforms in place and never advances them, which makes four basis frames comparable instead of four different moments. It is a String enum, not a bool, because the sweep sets exports from strings before _ready and a typed bool silently rejects "true" — the trap that has eaten fixture flags twice. `live` is the default and is the shipped behaviour, so no placement sees the pin.
dna.default: generator=perlin - the perlin branch of the shader's dispatch is the shipped noise2d body, character for character (diffed against HEAD, not eyeballed), and _apply_generator writes 1 into a uniform whose own declared default is already 1. Note the default is perlin and NOT simplex, the opposite of the bench artifacts, because that is what this file has always computed: hash2 returns a gradient per lattice corner and the interpolation dots it with the offset, which is Perlin's construction with a sine hash instead of a permutation table. MEASURED, not assumed: there are 13 mentions across 11 map files, not the 5 the promotion brief carried, by three reach-paths - bare tokens in Noise_6_Wall, Corridor_Noise_6_Wall, Noise_Functions, TestMap_Unused_23 and Walk_grande_galerie_axial_text; `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:shader_noise_space` in six museum trials, where the token is the furniture's mount value and the # keys are the furniture's; and `perlin_noise->shader_noise_space` in Trial_erosion_noise, which is a transformation target and not a config. None carries a generator key, and apply_grid_config returns unless a token names a word this file knows AND that word differs from the one it holds.
dna.was: seven exports, every one of them a rate or a toggle on the animation loop, and the runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The decision that carries the argument was not an export at all: it was the body of a single function called noise2d, hard-coded to one basis in a room whose walls, ceiling and floor are made of nothing else.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: perlin_noise, simplex_noise, noise_terrain - `generator` is the same axis with the same four values in the same order. The noise sequence is built on comparing bases; spelling the comparison a second way would leave nothing to compare. cellular, not worley, for the same reason. What differs here is the scale of the question: on the bench a basis is a tabletop of displaced cubes you look down at, and here it is the room you are standing inside.
dna.amplitude_note: The four bases are AMPLITUDE-MATCHED rather than merely swapped in. Measured over 30,000 samples each returns mean |value| = 0.137, which is what the shipped perlin returns; the three scaling constants in the shader (0.770, 38.0, 0.827) exist only for that. Without them the sweep would mostly have been reading which basis is BRIGHTER once the six-octave sum is pushed through smoothstep(0.2, 0.8), and the axis would have been about exposure instead of about structure. Their own characters survive the matching: measured local step per unit distance is 4.7% of mean for value, 8.4% perlin, 11.0% cellular, 13.9% simplex.
dna.declined: animation_speed (this file's own declared critical_parameter until now), time_scale_variation, color_cycle_speed and density_variation - four rates, all real, all audible in the room, and all invisible to one still. Promoting any of them would have produced the info_board result: a finished-looking experiment answering nothing. `octaves` was also declined despite simplex_noise carrying it as a numeric axis: the fbm here runs six octaves over a wall two metres from the eye, so the lower rungs would read as a blurrier wall rather than as a claim about self-similarity, and one honest axis is worth more than a second one that argues about resolution.
dna.still_note: the basis is a fragment-shader uniform, so it is resolved every frame and never settles into geometry — but it is also constant in time under the fixture, so one frame is a complete account. The subject is a closed 16 x 12 x 27 m box of CSGBox3D walls with cull_disabled, so the sweep's camera sits outside and photographs two or three wall faces filling the frame. That is the field at full size, which is the best case for measuring a basis; if the bite comes back small, suspect the clock, not the axis.
dna.finding: QueerNoiseShader.gdshader and WallNoiseShader.gdshader were BYTE-IDENTICAL, header comment included — the room-sphere shader carried the wall shader's filename at the top of the file. The @identity's claim that 'the two materials run independent shader noise loops' out of phase is one shader run twice with different uniform values and a 0.7x offset on time. Both files now carry the same dispatch so the room and its walls change basis together.

shader_noise_space.description: Interactive shader-based noise space exploration with procedural textures and patterns
shader_noise_space.name: Shader Noise Space
shader_noise_space.qfep_connection: Noise evaluated per-pixel at framerate: the GPU as noise organ, procedural texture with no texture stored. The room turns as you move because nothing in it is a picture — everything is a function, sampled where you look.

shannon_entropy_meter.description: Wall-mounted Shannon entropy gauge — generates a random sequence, computes symbol frequencies, and displays H = -Σ p(x) log₂ p(x). Bar gauge fills from 0 to max entropy (~3.32 bits for 10 symbols). Frequency histogram shows symbol distribution.
shannon_entropy_meter.name: Shannon Entropy Meter
