simplex_noise.description: Interactive Simplex noise generation and visualization for high-quality procedural content
simplex_noise.name: Simplex Noise
simplex_noise.qfep_connection: Perlin's own second draft: the simplex grid replaces squares, fewer artifacts, better behavior in high dimensions. Standing beside its ancestor it teaches versioning as a mathematical practice — even noise gets revised.

dna.default: disclosure=works - the shipped machine byte for byte: the seated side screen at its shipped 0.150 m, the counts, the Reel 1 histogram, the Theory 2.8% line, and the resting text 'Pulls: 0 / Pull the lever!'. All 14 existing placements are untouched, and apply_grid_config only rebuilds when a value actually changed and only after _ready has built once.
dna.was: a slot machine with no turnable knob at all - apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`, so all 14 rooms held one identical machine, and the odds it embodies (6^3 = 216, P(triple) = 6/216) were only ever inferable from a histogram nobody had pulled yet
dna.note: the family's word, not a new one: coin_toss, prng_crank_machine, monte_carlo_dartboard, trng_vs_prng, shannon_entropy_meter, hardware_entropy_decay, random_number_book_page_1955 and env_one all carry `disclosure`, and the ladder + its ranks are read out of prng_crank_machine.gd rather than copied. Each rung builds its own RESTING face (blanked plate / short screen / ruled paper / shipped screen / odds board) because the evidence is one still at zero pulls - a text-only ladder would render five identical frames. spin_seed=0 is the engine RNG exactly as shipped; the fixture pins it only for capture.
dna.declines: spin_speed, stop_delay and AUTO_INTERVAL are the obvious knobs and all three are time-domain, invisible to a still

slot_machine.description: A classic slot machine with 3 spinning reels. Pull the VR lever to spin — reels stop one by one, left to right. Tracks a histogram of symbol frequencies showing convergence to uniform distribution. Triple matches flash gold. AUTO mode for rapid sampling.
slot_machine.name: Slot Machine
slot_machine.qfep_connection: Independence — each reel is an independent uniform trial. The combination space grows multiplicatively (6^3 = 216 outcomes).

spawn_randomcubes.description: Interactive 3D Jackson Pollock-inspired painting using movement-based procedural randomness
spawn_randomcubes.name: spawn_randomcubes
spawn_randomcubes.qfep_connection: Cubes are dealt at random intervals, drift on rails, and are deleted past a boundary, with a breakage routine ready to turn any of them into eight fragments. A population rather than objects: each cube is disposable because the distribution that issued it persists.

ten_print.description: Interactive recreation of the classic Commodore 64 10 PRINT maze generation algorithm
ten_print.name: 10 PRINT
ten_print.qfep_connection: The C64 one-liner, but with its coin rigged: the slash-or-backslash probability breathes between 0.2 and 0.8 on a slow sine as the maze writes itself row by row. The rule never changes — only the fairness of the coin, and that alone re-textures the whole labyrinth.

ten_print_maze_3d.description: Extrudes the classic 10 PRINT pattern into a standing maze and animates an ant pathfinder through it.
ten_print_maze_3d.name: ten_print_maze_3d
ten_print_maze_3d.qfep_connection: The 10 PRINT coin flip stood up into walls that keep re-rolling on a timer, while an ant recomputes its route through them: one bit per cell is enough to turn navigation into a live negotiation instead of a solved map.

tessellation_lattice_demo.description: Random walk on tessellated lattice structures (triangular, hexagonal, square), showing how tiling geometry affects diffusion patterns.
tessellation_lattice_demo.name: Tessellation Lattice Demo

dna.default: cell=cube, adjacency=face - cube resolves to TessellationType.CUBE, which is the value the enum already held and the only one tessellation_lattice_demo.tscn has ever written; face returns the same six orthogonal offsets _get_unvisited_neighbors used to hard-code. Both apply_grid_config hooks (the root pass-through and the child) rebuild only on a CHANGED value and only after _ready, and neither of the 2 existing placements sends any config, so Mosaic_Pattern_Maker and TestMap_Unused_27 are byte-identical to before.
dna.was: the four space-filling solids were an int enum called tessellation_type, reachable only from four Buttons in a desktop CanvasLayer that VR never shows and the capture bench hides - a map token could not set it at all, because config values arrive as STRINGS and a typed int property rejects "2" silently. The walk's neighbourhood was six literal Vector3i offsets inside _get_unvisited_neighbors, identical for all four solids, so the registry's claim that this shows 'how tiling geometry affects diffusion patterns' was not true of the code.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03 - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, and it was right about the ROOT: the scene root runs tessellation_demo_controller.gd, whose apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`, so every export on the TessellationLatticeWalk child was unreachable from any map token. The root now forwards. FIXTURE IS LOAD-BEARING, twice over. random_seed was 0 (= do not seed) and the walk calls randi(), so without pinning it three lattices would be three different walks and the comparison would measure noise. show_all_at_start matters because the reveal is TIME-DRIVEN at 10 cells/sec: at the bench's 1.1 s settle a still would catch about eleven cells out of 512 and every tile would look like the same handful of specks. Setting that flag also had to stop the auto-walk in code - reveal_all leaves the index at the end of the path, and the next _process tick took the loop_walk branch and hid everything it had just revealed. adjacency is the weaker of the two axes ON PURPOSE and its weakness is honest: a still cannot photograph a path, only the colour field the path leaves behind, since each revealed cell is tinted by its index along the walk. If the critic reports adjacency faint, that is a fact about the still, not about the axis. cell should be violent - it changes the shape of all 512 solids at once.
dna.kin: vector_field_visualizer.lattice is a different question wearing a similar word: there `lattice` is the scaffold a field is SAMPLED on (square | polar | hidden), a way of making the invisible visible. Here the tessellating solid IS the subject, not the scaffold, so it takes the code's own noun - cell_mesh, cell_size, 'Total Cells' - rather than borrowing a word that would imply the two artifacts measure alike.

tessellation_lattice_demo.qfep_connection: The tessellation exists whole before the first cell appears: a shuffled walk path merely grants visibility, one space-filling polyhedron at a time, then loops and forgets. Discovery staged over a fully determined lattice — chance decides only the order of appearance, never what there is.

trng_vs_prng.description: Interactive comparison between True Random Number Generators and Pseudo-Random Number Generators
trng_vs_prng.name: TRNG vs PRNG
trng_vs_prng.qfep_connection: The chapter's founding trial: the crank versus the harvest. A PRNG is determinism wearing a costume — same seed, same sequence, forever replayable. A TRNG listens to the world (decay, thermal hiss) and cannot repeat itself even if asked. Standing between them you learn that most computed randomness is a performance of freedom, and real entropy has to be gathered, not made.

value_noise.description: Interactive Value noise generation and visualization for procedural texture creation
value_noise.name: Value Noise
value_noise.qfep_connection: Randomness lives only on the lattice; everything between is interpolation, and the sliders let you swap None for Linear for Smoothstep over the very same dice rolls. Smoothness exposed as a post-production decision — the noise never changed, only your policy for the gaps.

voxelnoise.description: 3D noise visualized as voxels — cubes appear or disappear based on noise threshold, revealing the underlying scalar field as solid geometry.
voxelnoise.name: Voxel Noise
voxelnoise.qfep_connection: 3D noise made walkable census: cubes appear where the field crosses threshold, vanish where it does not. The invisible correlation structure of the noise stands revealed as architecture — you are looking at the field's memory, cell by cell.

walk_random.description: An algorithmic walker that creates trails through the grid space
walk_random.name: Random Walker
walk_random.qfep_connection: The walker doesn't render a trail — it edits the map, placing and removing real structure cubes through the grid system as it drifts inside its clamped 8×8 yard. Chance is granted write-access to the floor, but on a lease: twenty cubes long, then the oldest is repossessed.

walkingsphere.description: Spike, Random walk, Cellular automata  sphere
walkingsphere.name: walkingsphere
walkingsphere.qfep_connection: Seven deformation regimes — ordered spikes through random walk to cellular automata — take turns on the same sphere, which keeps books on its own volume and total displacement: E_flux with an accountant, so order and chance can be compared by what each spends of the surface.

worley_noise.description: Voronoi/cellular noise texture on a floor quad. Scatters random seed points and computes F2-F1 (second-nearest minus nearest distance) for the classic cell boundary look. Complement to Perlin/Simplex noise.
worley_noise.name: Worley Noise

seed_replay_demo.name: Seed Replay Demo
seed_replay_demo.description: Demonstrates seed reproducibility — an 8x8 grid of colored cubes generated from a seed. Same seed always produces the same pattern. Slider changes seed, Replay regenerates identically, Random picks a new seed.

dna.default: comparison=single - one column at the shipped origin_x (-col_w / 2.0, which is what the n-column formula collapses to at n == 1), no caption Label3D created at all, the headline reading the shipped 'SEED: %d', and the cubes coloured by _rng seeded to seed_value = 42, the number _current_seed was born with, consumed in the same row-major order. The 7 direct placements and the 85 exhibit_furniture#mount:seed_replay_demo mounts are all bare tokens - no map_data.json anywhere sends this artifact a config dict - and apply_grid_config, which was literally `pass` before today, now returns early unless a value differs AND _ready has already built.
dna.was: no axis, and apply_grid_config implemented as `pass`. Four exports and all four were grid geometry (cols, rows, cube size, gap). The seed itself was a plain var, not an export, so nothing outside the artifact could reach it.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. THIS ARTIFACT'S SUBJECT IS THE SWEEP'S OWN METHODOLOGY, which is why the axis had to be about evidence and not about the seed. The shipped object asserts 'same seed, same grid' and photographs badly, because one grid is one grid: a still of a seeded 8x8 and a still of an UNSEEDED 8x8 are indistinguishable, so the picture contains no evidence for the claim written on it. comparison gives the claim a second panel. replicas runs the same seed twice side by side and the two grids are identical - the control, and the only value that shows the property the artifact is named for. seeds runs 42 against contrast_seed 137. ladder runs three consecutive seeds, because adjacent integers are not adjacent worlds and that is the fact a slider hides. Captions appear per column only when there is something to compare, so `single` gains no node. TWO VALUES WERE CONSIDERED AND DECLINED. `unseeded` - two grids from randomize(), differing despite the same label, the exact failure this corpus keeps hitting - is the best picture of the four and cannot be shipped: it would make one tile a sample instead of a fact, and CLAUDE.md's own gotcha table lists 'strong confident bite on a generative artifact = unseeded randf' as a harness misdiagnosis, so declaring a value that deliberately triggers it would poison the next reader's verdict. `blind` - one grid with the seed withheld - is a real argument but it compares nothing, and taking the word `comparison` for it would be the science_screen fault in slow motion. SEED IS NOT AN AXIS: a seed ladder is what the artifact already was.
dna.kin: distribution_comparator.comparison (rules|replicas|tails|counts) sits one entry away in this same file and `replicas` is taken from it character for character, meaning exactly what it means there: the same generator run again, as the control for a claim about difference. The two should measure alike and the shipped states rhyme - both artifacts had apply_grid_config as a no-op and a sign making a claim the machine could not evidence. The rest of the list differs because the claims differ: distribution_comparator asks which LAW produced a histogram, this one asks whether the same INPUT produces the same output. space_filling_curve_gallery.comparison (grammars|depths|overlay|single) is the third declaration of the word and `single` is taken from there unchanged - one panel, nothing beside it.

dna.default: comparison=rules, evidence=sample - rules rebuilds the shipped uniform/gaussian/exponential lineup in the same order with the same three colours (the palette is now keyed by law, and at rules that is the old positional blue/green/orange exactly), and evidence=sample is 1000 draws, the number _sample_count was born with. Every one of the 34 map placements is a bare token or a rotation/offset token - no config token in any map_data.json can reach these axes - so all of them render unchanged.
dna.was: three hard-coded columns and a hard-coded 1000 draws, with apply_grid_config() implemented as `pass`. The sign says ONE SOURCE - THREE RULES and the machine could never show the control for that claim: one rule three times, which is what replicas is.
dna.note: fixture pins the draw (evidence_seed defaults to -1 = randomize, the legacy stream); without it two frames of the same variant are two different histograms and the sweep measures the dice. The evidence list is declared richest-first ON PURPOSE: a 4x4 cross exceeds the sweep's default --max=9 and the sweeper trims from the END of each value list, so an ascending list would have crossed all four lineups against an empty chart and a one-draw chart. Same set, same code, informative under truncation - run --max=16 for the full cross. Deliberately not promoted: RESAMPLE and the exponential rate - a button press is time-domain and lambda only slides one column's mass along its own axis.

distribution_comparator.name: Distribution Comparator
distribution_comparator.description: Side-by-side comparison of 3 probability distributions — Uniform (blue), Gaussian (green), Exponential (orange). Three columns of 16 histogram bars generated from the same sample count. Slider scales samples from 100 to 10000; resample button regenerates all three.
distribution_comparator.qfep_connection: Three distributions from one random source — the channeling rule (F) determines shape. Uniform is maximum entropy; Gaussian is the attractor of summation; Exponential is memoryless decay. Same randomness, different constraints, different forms.

perlin_noise_bridge.description: Side-by-side 16x16 heightfield grids comparing white noise (chaotic) and Perlin noise (terrain-like). Shows how gradient noise transforms raw randomness into coherent structure through spatial memory.
perlin_noise_bridge.name: Perlin Noise Bridge

reaction_diffusion_intro.description: A 32x32 Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion simulation rendered as an ImageTexture. Two chemicals U and V interact to produce spots, stripes, or coral patterns from random initial conditions — Turing morphogenesis made visible.
reaction_diffusion_intro.name: Reaction-Diffusion Intro

rejection_toy.name: Rejection Toy (held - under the curve)
rejection_toy.description: Hand-scale rejection sampling: dots scattered in a box, the ones under the target curve kept (green), the rest refused. Sample any shape by throwing away what does not fit.

rejection_bench.name: Rejection Bench (accept / reject)
rejection_bench.description: Bench rejection sampling: darts fill a panel under a target curve, accepted ones build a histogram of the shape beside it.

rejection_room.name: Rejection Room (walk-in accept / reject)
rejection_room.description: Room-scale rejection sampling: a giant target curve, darts raining through the volume, accepted ones glowing into the distribution on the floor.

pi_dart_toy.name: Pi Dart Toy (held Monte Carlo)
pi_dart_toy.description: Hand-scale Monte Carlo: darts speckle a square with an inscribed quarter-circle; the inside/total ratio estimates pi. Estimate the unknowable by throwing enough darts.

pi_dart_bench.name: Pi Dart Bench (pi convergence)
pi_dart_bench.description: Bench Monte Carlo: hundreds of darts accumulate and a convergence line tightens the running pi estimate toward 3.14159.

pi_dart_room.name: Pi Dart Room (stand in the square)
pi_dart_room.description: Room-scale Monte Carlo: you stand in the unit square as darts rain - inside the circle green, outside red - and the floor ratio reads pi.

coin_dice_bench.name: Coin & Dice Bench (discrete tallies)
coin_dice_bench.description: Bench of discrete chance: a flipping coin and a tumbling die feed two live bar charts that trend toward uniform.

dice_rain_room.name: Dice Rain Room (raining histogram)
dice_rain_room.description: Room-scale discrete chance: dice rain from the ceiling and settle into six columns by face, building a roughly flat (uniform) histogram.

random_walk_bench.name: Random Walk Bench (drunkard path)
random_walk_bench.description: Bench random walk: a token steps at random across a tabletop grid, trailing the path it has wandered - each step a fresh coin.

distribution_bench.name: Distribution Bench (live histogram)
distribution_bench.description: Bench distribution: beads fall into bins and a twelve-bar histogram holds its shape - not all outcomes are equal.

perlin_bench.name: Perlin Bench (coherent curve)
perlin_bench.description: Bench Perlin noise: a smooth, coherent 1D curve flows across a panel with a marker riding it - noise with neighbours.

noise_compare_bench.name: Noise Compare Bench (value / simplex / worley)
noise_compare_bench.description: Bench comparison of three coherent noises side by side - value, simplex, and worley - so their textures read against each other.

noise_displacer.name: Noise Displacer (surface displacement)
noise_displacer.description: A tool: a simplex field displacing a flat surface into rolling hills in real time. Coherent noise doing the job of shaping geometry.

noise_flow_drones.name: Noise Flow Drones (flow-field navigation)
noise_flow_drones.description: A swarm steered by a Perlin flow field - the noise field doing the real job of navigation, each drone reading the value at its feet.

noise_height_toy.name: Noise Height Toy (held heightfield)
noise_height_toy.description: The smallest 'noise = height': a little tile of cells whose heights come from a noise field, undulating in the hand.

noise_dunes_bench.name: Noise Dunes Bench (tabletop landscape)
noise_dunes_bench.description: Bench landscape: a noise field read as height becomes drifting dunes, low sand to pale ridge.

noise_terrain_forge.name: Noise Terrain Forge (stamps ground)
noise_terrain_forge.description: A tool: a forge that stamps a walkable noise-terrain patch - turning a noise field into usable ground.

blue_noise_toy.name: Blue Noise Toy (even-spaced points)
blue_noise_toy.description: Hand-scale blue noise: points placed by best-candidate so each keeps its distance - random without clumping.

blue_noise_bench.name: Blue Noise Bench (white vs blue)
blue_noise_bench.description: Bench comparison: the same count of points placed as white noise (clumpy) and blue noise (even) side by side.

blue_noise_planter.name: Blue Noise Planter (even placement)
blue_noise_planter.description: A tool: scattering props with blue-noise spacing so they never clump - even placement doing a real job.

seed_toy.name: Seed Toy (same seed, same glyph)
seed_toy.description: Hand-scale determinism: a seed dial grows a glyph; the same seed always grows the same one - pseudo-randomness in disguise.

seed_bench.name: Seed Bench (same seed, same stream)
seed_bench.description: Bench determinism: two generators fed the same seed produce identical streams; flip one bit and they diverge forever.

entropy_bench.name: Entropy Bench (bits of surprise)
entropy_bench.description: Bench entropy: a biasable source whose Shannon entropy reads from one bit at fair down toward zero as the bias grows.

markov_melody.name: Markov Melody (chain composes)
markov_melody.description: A tool: a Markov chain hopping a ring of note-states to compose a melody - the memoryless chain doing real work.

jitter_bench.name: Jitter Bench (perturb the grid)
jitter_bench.description: Bench of random transforms: a tidy grid of cubes dissolved from order into noise as the jitter dial rises.

ten_print_toy.name: Ten Print Toy (maze of slashes)
ten_print_toy.description: Hand-scale 10 PRINT: one coin-flip per cell draws a slash or backslash, and a maze appears - the smallest generative grammar.

ten_print_bench.name: Ten Print Bench (bias dial)
ten_print_bench.description: Bench 10 PRINT: a larger maze panel whose character shifts as a slash/backslash probability dial biases the coin.

dna.default: odds=0.5, alphabet=diagonals - 0.5 is the literal `_rng.randf() < 0.5` fair coin and diagonals returns the same box at the same rotation.z = +/-PI*0.25, so all 7 placements weave exactly the cloth they wove before; apply_grid_config is now guarded and rebuilds only on a real change (it previously tore the loom down on every call, and on a pre-_ready call it built the bolt twice)
dna.was: a hard-coded fair coin between two hard-coded +/-45 degree bars. The only exports were cols and rows - the size of the bolt, not what it says.
dna.fixture_note: weave_seed pins the flip so five odds tiles differ by their bias and not by five different draws; weaving false freezes the scroll so a still is one cloth rather than one mid-scroll frame. Both default to the shipped behaviour (seed 0 = randomize, weaving on).
dna.vocabulary_note: alphabet is taken from GeneticProgramming.alphabet - the symbol set a generator draws from - which is precisely the question here. odds is a new word: bias was already spent on pixel_cloud for a spatial lean (rise/none/spire/sprawl) and chance on random_cubes for WHICH property is randomised, neither of which is the weighting of a coin. panel_bridge_loom's threading_draw / treadling_order were considered and declined: those name a deterministic weaving draft, and this loom's whole content is that there is no draft, only a flip.
dna.declined: scroll rate and row cadence (_step 0.18 s) are time-domain and invisible to a still; cols and rows are size.

ten_print_textile.name: Ten Print Textile (fabric loom)
ten_print_textile.description: A tool: 10 PRINT as a textile loom, weaving an endless bolt of slash/backslash fabric - the pattern doing a design job.

scatter_bench.name: Scatter Bench (Pollock drips)
scatter_bench.description: Bench of generative art: chance as a brush, flinging drips and splatters across a canvas at bench scale.

random_fireworks.name: Random Fireworks (per-particle chance)
random_fireworks.description: A tool: fireworks whose particles each get their own random velocity and colour - individual chance making an emergent display.

lottery_drum.name: Lottery Drum (uniform raffle)
lottery_drum.description: A tool: a tumbling raffle drum ejecting one numbered ball, each equally likely - uniform RNG doing a real picking job.

dna_sprout.name: DNA Sprout (held seed -> plant)
dna_sprout.description: The held end of seed -> form: a deterministic CritterDNA genome grown by an L-system into one plant. Same seed always grows the same plant - the deep seed, not flat randomness. Bridges seed_toy to the DNA galleries.

genome_bench.name: Genome Bench (scrub -> regrow)
genome_bench.description: Bench genotype-to-phenotype: a CritterDNA genome drifts by small mutations and the plant re-grows each change. The row of gene-bars is the seed - store the numbers and the form returns.

seed_vs_random.name: Seed vs Random (the thesis bed)
seed_vs_random.description: The payoff: two beds. LEFT grows from fresh randomness every few seconds - never the same, nothing to store. RIGHT grows from fixed CritterDNA seeds - store the seed, regrow it exactly. Flat randomness vs the deep, side by side.

galton_friction.description: Two solutions to the Galton bell side by side — THE HARVEST (real physics, a falling body, lumpy and never repeating) vs THE CRANK (pseudo, bin = sum(randf() < 0.5), instant and perfect and reproducible). The crank is smaller because it is cheaper: real randomness is too expensive or too specific to keep everywhere.
galton_friction.name: Galton Friction
galton_friction.qfep_connection: The manufactured vs the harvested — real randomness is expensive and specific; what the system holds is the crank. The bell you trust is almost always made.
